cards.def: A five-time married cloth-maker who argues from experience for wives' sovereignty over husbands and tells a romance that rewards that grant.
The Wife's fifth husband, a young clerk who nightly reads her antifeminist texts until their fight ends with him burning the book and giving her the bridle.
A rapist knight whose life depends on learning what women most desire, then must marry the old wife who taught him and finally yield her governaunce.
The foul old woman who gives the knight the sovereignty answer, lectures him on gentilesse, and becomes fair and good once given maistry.
A convent head whose courtly manners, Stratford French, pity for pets and "Amor vincit omnia" brooch let admiration for refinement also read as worldly vanity.
A hunting outrider who scorns the old Rule and cloister texts, while the narrator agrees "his opinion was good," so praise of his horsemanship also marks a monk out of place.
A merry limitour praised as virtuous and "the beste beggar," whose easy penance for gifts and avoidance of lepers let skill and corruption share one portrait.
